title: Integrated Approach to Chronic Pain—The Role of Psychosocial Factors and Multidisciplinary Treatment: A Narrative Review
authors: Irena Kovačević; Jadranka Pavić; Biljana Filipović; Štefanija Ozimec Vulinec; Boris Ilić; Davorina Petek; Cesar Fernández-de-las-Peñas
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
pain_condition_detail: chronic non-malignant pain, including chronic lower back pain, neuropathic pain, musculoskeletal pain, inflammatory pain, mechanical/compression pain
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the biopsychosocial model as an organizing principle and intervention rationale, describing it as a framework for multidisciplinary rehabilitation. It lists biological, psychological, and social factors but does not specify mechanisms linking them. The model is invoked to justify multidisciplinary treatment rather than to explain pain pathways.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper asserts associations between social factors (support, SES, relationships) and pain outcomes, and between psychological factors (beliefs, distress) and pain, but does not specify pathways or mechanisms linking domains.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper advocates for a biopsychosocial model but provides no mechanism linking biological, psychological, and social domains, they are listed in parallel
conceptual_tensions_2: Social factors are acknowledged as important but are not elaborated beyond listing, the paper is psych-dominant in actual content
conceptual_tensions_3: The paper uses 'biopsychosocial' and 'multidisciplinary' almost interchangeably, conflating the model with the treatment approach
additional_observations_1: The paper is a narrative review with no systematic search or quality assessment, limiting the strength of its claims
additional_observations_2: The paper cites Engel's biopsychosocial model but does not engage with its theoretical depth or critiques
additional_observations_3: The paper mentions ICD-11 classification and IASP definition but does not integrate these into the BPS analysis
synthesis_note: This narrative review uses the biopsychosocial label extensively to justify multidisciplinary treatment, but operationalizes it as a list of separate components. Psychological content is elaborated (beliefs, attitudes, coping), while biological and social factors are mentioned but not developed. No cross-domain mechanisms are proposed, and the triadic integration is absent. The paper contributes to the finding that BPS language is widespread while substantive integration is not.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because all three domains are present but social and biological are thin, and no integration is specified. Triadic integration is 'none' because domains are listed in parallel. Psych-dominant because psychological content occupies most of the results.

authors: Irena Kovačević; Jadranka Pavić; Biljana Filipović; Štefanija Ozimec Vulinec; Boris Ilić; Davorina Petek; Cesar Fernández-de-las-Peñas
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
pain_condition_detail: Chronic non-malignant pain, with examples of chronic primary pain, chronic secondary musculoskeletal pain, chronic neuropathic pain, chronic postsurgical/posttraumatic pain, and low back pain.
context_note: Cites European and U.S. adult prevalence and discusses primary healthcare access, healthcare-system sustainability, and multidisciplinary pain centers.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_usage_sections: abstract; conclusion; discussion; introduction; methods; other
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the BPS label mainly to justify multidisciplinary chronic pain treatment: physical training/patient education, CBT/psychological interventions, and work/social-environment discussions are listed as components. It does not test or specify a three-domain mechanism.
integration_mechanism_summary: No explicit cross-domain mechanism is proposed. The paper asserts interactions and treatment effects, with directional claims such as psychological impact on pain intensity and social support on activation/pain tolerance, but pathways and mediators are not specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: Chronic pain is defined by duration in more than one way: exceeding expected recovery, lasting more than three months, or lasting longer than six months
conceptual_tensions_2: The paper invokes a complex biopsychosocial interplay but mostly lists biological, psychological, and social factors or interventions side by side
conceptual_tensions_3: The umbrella term chronic non-malignant pain covers chronic primary, secondary musculoskeletal, neuropathic, postsurgical/posttraumatic, headache/orofacial, visceral, and cancer-related categories
conceptual_tensions_4: Psychological constructs receive definitions or operational tools more often than social constructs, despite the paper calling for greater social emphasis
conceptual_tensions_5: The review evaluates treatment approaches through a non-systematic narrative method without reporting formal quality or risk-of-bias appraisal
additional_observations_1: The paper positions chronic pain as a human right and global public health priority
additional_observations_2: The search strategy includes MeSH terms Chronic Pain, Pain Management, and Models, Biopsychosocial
additional_observations_3: Virtual reality is introduced as promising but preliminary, not synthesized as an established BPS component
additional_observations_4: Multidisciplinary team composition is specified, but the team model is not evaluated as an implementation mechanism
additional_observations_5: Primary healthcare is framed as the access point for early treatment and return to work
additional_observations_6: The review reports 120 papers but does not provide a formal synthesis method or appraisal results
synthesis_note: This narrative review operationalizes BPS mainly as a clinical rationale for multidisciplinary chronic pain management. It names biological, psychological, and social factors and interventions, but the domains are mostly asserted or listed rather than connected through explicit mechanisms.
coding_rationale: BPS label primarily justifies multidisciplinary care; all domains present but mostly parallel/asserted. Triadic integration is descriptive, not mechanistic.

citation: Kovačević et al. (2024), International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
title: Integrated Approach to Chronic Pain—The Role of Psychosocial Factors and Multidisciplinary Treatment: A Narrative Review
authors: Irena Kovačević; Jadranka Pavić; Biljana Filipović; Štefanija Ozimec Vulinec; Boris Ilić; Davorina Petek; Cesar Fernández-de-las-Peñas
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes the results section into thematic categories (prevalence, risk factors, attitudes/beliefs, treatment) and uses BPS as an overarching framework for multidisciplinary treatment without specifying integration mechanisms between domains.
emergent_labels_1: primary and secondary classification of chronic pain
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS is presented as essential framework but lacks specified mechanisms for domain integration
conceptual_tensions_2: Paper acknowledges need for greater emphasis on psychological/social factors despite advocating BPS approach
additional_observations_1: Paper uses non-systematic narrative review methodology rather than systematic review
additional_observations_2: Includes both foundational literature (83 papers) and recent publications (37 papers from 2018-2023)
additional_observations_3: Emphasizes multidisciplinary treatment teams with three doctors and various health professionals
synthesis_note: This narrative review advocates for the biopsychosocial model as an organizing framework for chronic pain treatment but does not specify mechanisms for integration between biological, psychological, and social domains. It identifies risk factors across all three domains and describes multidisciplinary treatment approaches, yet the BPS label functions primarily as a structural organizing principle rather than an integrative explanatory framework.
coding_rationale: BPS typology as 'multifactorial' because all three domains are substantively present with named constructs, but integration scored as 'none' because no cross-domain mechanisms are specified. Domain coverage as 'mentioned' because each domain has at least one named construct but is not developed into a sustained analytical thread.
